mechanism_narrative: A declining federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where FEDFUNDS has declined for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 7.0% for two consecutive months, it indicates a weakening labor market that typically precedes economic slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE has exceeded 7.0% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals strong consumer demand and economic activity, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint increase in HOUST and RSAFS fails to produce positive 5-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or the correlation between the joint signal and returns is not statistically significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 230 (index value), the Federal Reserve typically responds with tighter monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods where CPIAUCSL exceeds 230.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 100.0 for three consecutive months indicates robust manufacturing activity, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where INDPRO has been above 100.0 for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in non-farm payrolls below 135,000 thousand for two consecutive months signals weakening labor market conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where PAYEMS has been below 135000 for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in non-farm payrolls and increase in unemployment rate signals a deteriorating labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition of PAYEMS declining and UNRATE rising fails to produce negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or the correlation between the joint signal and returns is not statistically significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real sales above 425,000 million dollars for two consecutive months signals strong consumer spending, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where RSAFS has exceeded 425000 for two consecutive months.
